competency_fulfillment.rationale: Completing a figure is the competency's object, yet eight of nine samples mirror a single point or one polygon vertex across the line. Only the butterfly touches a figure, and it asks for a count of dots on the right wing rather than for the missing half to be built.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both orientations of the line of symmetry occur, mirroring is asked left-to-right and right-to-left as well as above-to-below, the reflected object is sometimes a point and sometimes a polygon vertex, and the distances used span 2 to 5 units.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The governing principle is stated in terms a Grade 3 pupil can act on, that each vertex on the second half must be the same distance from the line of symmetry as its partner on the first half, and all counting is in whole grid units.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Two stems repeat word for word within the nine samples, the 3-units-left item and the 2-units-above item, and every sample is multiple choice. The butterfly is the only concrete object in the set; the rest are abstract points on an unnamed grid.

competency_alignment.rationale: The wrong options are built from the actual misconceptions of this skill rather than from noise: the doubled distance appears as 6 grid units to the right of the line, and placing the partner on the line itself or on the same side both appear, so choosing correctly requires the mirror idea.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Distances of 2 to 5 grid units keep every reflection countable on ordinary grid paper, which is the right magnitude for completing a symmetric figure by hand at this grade.
